question.problem:
Consider the standard matrices of three linear transformations shown below. Which of the transformations map ${R}^{2}$ onto the whole of ${R}^{2}?$

$$
{T}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}],\,{T}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,{T}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
Given a linear transformation over ${R}^{2}$ with the standard matrix $T,$ we have the following:

- $T$ maps ${R}^{2}$ onto ${R}^{2}$ if and only if $\text{rank}(T)=2,$ i.e., $T$ is nonsingular.

- $T$ maps ${R}^{2}$ onto a line if and only if $\text{rank}(T)=1.$

- $T$ maps ${R}^{2}$ onto $(0,0)$ if and only if $\text{rank}(T)=0,$ i.e., $T$ is the zero matrix.

With that in mind, let's examine our matrices.

- ${T}_{1}$ maps ${R}^{2}$ onto ${R}^{2}.$ Indeed, ${T}_{1}$ is a nonsingular matrix, i.e. $\text{rank}({T}_{1})=2.$

- ${T}_{2}$ maps ${R}^{2}$ onto $(0,0)$ since ${T}_{2}$ is the zero matrix, i.e. $\text{rank}({T}_{2})=0.$

- ${T}_{3}$ maps ${R}^{2}$ onto a line. Notice that the columns of ${T}_{3}$ are linearly dependent but it's not the zero matrix. So, $\text{rank}({T}_{3})=1.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "${T}_{1}$ only."
